rationale: The hypothesis is explicitly conditional ("R&D pays *only when* cash flow is stable") but SUMRANK is a purely additive rank blend, so the signal will mostly be a 50/50 mixture of two separately known effects (R&D intensity and low cash-flow volatility) rather than the claimed interaction.

The multiplicative indicator gate genuinely implements the stated conditional logic and is internally consistent, though the large mass of exact zeros for non-persistent earners will make the short leg an unsorted lump and the construction is close to the known "R&D premium concentrated in profitable firms" result.

Cross-sectional variation in the denominator (intangibles plus cumulative R&D) dominates, so the ratio is effectively *short* intangible-intensive firms while the hypothesis argues intangible-rich firms are undervalued — a sign/mechanism contradiction — and firms with near-zero intangible capital produce explosive values.

This is an additive rank difference of two well-documented published anomalies (Sloan accruals and Eberhart-Maxwell-Siddique R&D increases) with no mechanism that makes the combination more than the sum of its parts, and the accrual leg will likely drive nearly all of the result.

Direction is internally coherent (high goodwill + weak cash flow + high leverage → negative slope) and the impairment-risk framing is economically sensible, but the nested SUMRANK yields an ad hoc 50/25/25 weighting and the low-cash-flow/high-leverage legs risk collapsing the signal into a generic distress proxy.

Same structural flaw as CashFlowStableRnD and largely redundant with it — an additive SUMRANK cannot express the claimed "ramp pays only inside stable-margin franchises" conditionality, and both legs (R&D increases, low fundamental volatility) are established standalone anomalies.
